summary: Reclassifies RFC 1863, a BGP/IDRP route server alternative to a full mesh, to Historic status, and obsoletes it. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo moves RFC 1863 to Historic status because its route-server design was not implemented or used as an alternative to full-mesh routing. It names other techniques that serve that purpose.

questions: what are alternatives to full mesh bgp
what did the rfc 1863 route server propose
subtitle: Reclassifies the RFC 1863 route-server proposal as Historic because it was not implemented or used.

tldr.problem: RFC 1863 described route servers as an alternative to full-mesh BGP/IDRP routing, but the memo says no implementation existed or was used for that purpose.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4223 moves RFC 1863 to Historic status and formally obsoletes it.
tldr.outcome: The memo names route reflectors, BGP confederations and private AS numbers as other techniques for avoiding full-mesh routing.

today: RFC 4223 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 1863, which it reclassifies as Historic. The unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes RFC 4223.

sections.title: The RFC 1863 Route-Server Proposal
sections.content: RFC 1863 describes using route servers as an alternative to BGP/IDRP full-mesh routing. RFC 4223 uses the term "RFC 1863 route server" only for a server specified by RFC 1863; other uses of the term are outside its scope.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 1863 proposed a route-server approach as an alternative to full-mesh routing. This memo discusses only that particular proposal.

sections.title: Reclassification to Historic
sections.content:
The memo states that implementations of RFC 1863 route servers do not exist and are not used as an alternative to full-mesh routing. It therefore reclassifies RFC 1863 as Historic and obsoletes it.

The memo also says IDRP for IP was never standardized by the IETF and can be considered obsolete. It distinguishes RFC 1863's route-server design from other route-server uses, which are outside its scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Because the design had not been implemented or used for its intended role, RFC 1863 is moved to Historic status. Other route-server uses are not covered by this decision.

sections.title: Other Techniques for Full-Mesh Alternatives
sections.content:
The memo lists BGP Route Reflectors (RFC 2796), BGP Confederations (RFC 3065) and private AS numbers as techniques that provide alternatives to full-mesh routing.

The RFC says reclassifying RFC 1863 has no security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo names route reflectors, confederations and private AS numbers as other alternatives to full-mesh routing.

references.text: Haskin, D., "A BGP/IDRP Route Server alternative to a full mesh routing", RFC 1863, October 1995.
Bates, T., Chandra, R., and E. Chen, "BGP Route Reflection - An Alternative to Full Mesh IBGP", RFC 2796, April 2000.
Traina, P., McPherson, D., and J. Scudder, "Autonomous System Confederations for BGP", RFC 3065, February 2001.
